messages.author: 82889e926eb5165e
messages.subject: plotProbe with no legend
parts:
Hi

I like the use of the function probe2WayMC, that it lets me do a Johnson-Neyman test, and that I can lot it with the plotProbe function. The problem is that with so many tested values when I plot them the legend its too large and it would better to not include include it. 

Is there a way to plotProbe without the legend?

Here is the example 

library(lavaan) 
library(semTools)

dat2wayMC <- indProd(dat2way, 1:3, 4:6)

model1 <- "
f1 =~ x1 + x2 + x3
f2 =~ x4 + x5 + x6
f12 =~ x1.x4 + x2.x5 + x3.x6
f3 =~ x7 + x8 + x9
f3 ~ f1 + f2 + f12
f12 ~~0*f1
f12 ~~ 0*f2
x1 ~ 0*1
x4 ~ 0*1
x1.x4 ~ 0*1
x7 ~ 0*1
f1 ~ NA*1
f2 ~ NA*1
f12 ~ NA*1
f3 ~ NA*1
"

fitMC2way <- sem(model1, data = dat2wayMC, std.lv = FALSE,
                 meanstructure = TRUE)
summary(fitMC2way)

result2wayMC <- probe2WayMC(fitMC2way, c("f1", "f2", "f12"),
                            "f3", "f2", seq(from=-3,to=3,by=.1))
result2wayMC

plotProbe(result2wayMC, xlim = c(-2, 2))

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: plotProbe with no legend
parts:
Mauricio,
  It is not pretty but the following approach worked.  (1) Make the required internal function available.  (2) Create a modified version of the function with no legend.  (3) Draw the graph with the modified function.  A more elegant approach might be to add a parameter to the function to suppress the legend.

Keith


plotSingleProbe <- semTools:::plotSingleProbe  # Make required internal function available



plotProbeNoLegend <-
function (object, xlim, xlab = "Indepedent Variable", ylab = "Dependent Variable",
    ...)
{
    if (length(xlim) != 2)
        stop("The x-limit should be specified as a numeric vector with the length of 2.")
    slope <- object$SimpleSlope
    numInt <- 2
    if (ncol(slope) == 6)
        numInt <- 3
    estSlope <- slope[, ncol(slope) - 3]
    estSlopeSig <- (slope[, ncol(slope)] < 0.05) + 1
    estIntercept <- NULL
    if (!is.null(object$SimpleIntcept))
        estIntercept <- object$SimpleIntcept[, ncol(slope) -
            3]
    if (numInt == 2) {
        plotSingleProbe(estSlope, estIntercept, xlim = xlim,
            xlab = xlab, ylab = ylab, colLine = estSlopeSig, ...)   # modified
#             legendMain = colnames(slope)[1], legendVal = slope[,  # commented out
#                1], ...)
               
                }
    else if (numInt == 3) {
        mod2 <- unique(slope[, 2])
        mod1 <- unique(slope[, 1])
        if (length(mod2) == 2) {
            obj <- par(mfrow = c(1, 2))
        }
        else if (length(mod2) == 3) {
            obj <- par(mfrow = c(1, 3))
        }
        else if (length(mod2) > 3) {
            obj <- par(mfrow = c(2, ceiling(length(mod2)/2)))
        }
        else if (length(mod2) == 1) {
        }
        else {
            stop("Some errors occur")
        }
        for (i in 1:length(mod2)) {
            select <- slope[, 2] == mod2[i]
            plotSingleProbe(estSlope[select], estIntercept[select],
                xlim = xlim, xlab = xlab, ylab = ylab, colLine = estSlopeSig[select],
                main = paste(colnames(slope)[2], "=", mod2[i]),
                legendMain = colnames(slope)[1], legendVal = mod1,
                ...)
        }
        if (length(mod2) > 1)
            par(obj)
    }
    else {
        stop("Please make sure that the object argument is obtained from 'probe2wayMC', 'probe2wayRC', 'probe3wayMC', or 'probe3wayRC'.")
    }
}


plotProbeNoLegend(result2wayMC, xlim = c(-2, 2))  # run graph with modified function


------------------------

Thanks Alex, and for posting a quick fix, Keith!

Alex, I won't have time for programming until February, so that's awesome if you have time earlier.  Because it is impossible to predict how (potentially horrible) plots will look in every situation, I am a fan of returning enough information for users to (re)construct the plot however they like.  So plotBrobe() could return a list instead of, well, nothing.  See the bottom of ?bsBootMiss for an example (source code is on line 154 of missingBootstrap.R).  Let me know if you think this is feasible for plotProbe(), too (maybe we make the change at the end of the hidden plotSingleProbe(), and make the default legend location optional to override with a new "legendLoc=" argument?).
